extracted.intended_audience: citizens, environmental groups, companies, and attorneys looking for EPA complaints and petitions for review
extracted.subtask_description: An official EPA Office of General Counsel page that publishes a searchable table of complaints and petitions for review received by EPA, with metadata (plaintiff(s), date, statute) and explanatory notes about interpretation and scope. Used by litigants and the public to locate filings and understand basic posting semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen suit provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the environmental statutes contain provisions that allow citizens to sue EPA when EPA allegedly fails to perform an act or mandatory duty required by the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement explains the legal basis for citizen-initiated complaints against EPA (i.e., suits for failure to perform nondiscretionary duties). It signals when a party might file a complaint but does not provide filing instructions or procedural requirements beyond asserting the existence of statutory citizen-suit provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for review in courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens may also file petitions for review in courts to challenge actions taken by EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes court petitions for review (judicial challenges to EPA action) from other types of petitions; implies a separate procedural path from citizen-suit complaints. No procedural steps provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of administrative and guidance petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative petitions for rulemaking and Guidance petitions are located on EPA’s Petitions Page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs users that petitions seeking rulemaking or guidance are handled via a different EPA resource (the Petitions Page) rather than on this complaints/petitions-for-review listing. Use that page for administrative petition submissions or searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting disclaimer regarding filing/service
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting does not mean that the notice was properly filed and/or served upon EPA or the United States, and EPA does not waive any defenses related to improper filing or service as it relates to the notices posted here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains limits of the public posting: listings are informational and may not reflect proper legal filing or service. Users should not assume that a posted document satisfies filing/service requirements or that EPA concedes any procedural defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table contents and usage notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The table below contains complaints and petitions for review received by EPA. Complaints are added as they are received. Many complaints include multiple parties or petitioners. Please use the search feature to search for complaints filed by a specific group or individual. Note that all links in the table below open in a new tab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes what the listing includes and how it is updated. Advises users to use the page search feature to find filings by party and warns that each link opens in a new tab. Useful operational guidance for locating documents but not procedural filing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date field semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: * For dates prior to October 16, 2017, the date shown is when EPA received the associated NOI, if applicable. Beginning October 16, 2017, the date shown is the date that the complaint was received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to interpret the 'Date' column depending on time period: earlier entries may show NOI receipt dates, later entries show complaint receipt dates. Important for temporal interpretation of listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute labeling and WOTUS explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: WOTUS means “waters of the United States” and is the term that generally defines the scope of federal protection of surface waters under the federal Clean Water Act. WOTUS litigation refers to challenges to rules defining that term issued by the EPA and the Department of the Army, Army Corps of Engineers. Both agencies administer permitting programs under the Clean Water Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies an abbreviation/label that appears in the 'Statute' column (e.g., 'CWA/WOTUS'). Helps readers interpret which laws or program terms are implicated by each listed complaint or petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute column (identifying applicable law)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listing includes a 'Statute' field (e.g., CAA, CWA, TSCA, APA, CERCLA, etc.) indicating the law(s) implicated by the complaint or petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute field identifies the legal basis or statutory authority at issue in a filing; readers should use that field to filter or locate matters under a particular statute. The page does not provide further guidance on statutory prerequisites or jurisdictional requirements for each statute.
